# pinecone_invite (Data Source)

Fetch a single invite by ID. Unlike the `pinecone_invites` list, which returns only `pending` and `expired` invites, this returns an invite in any state — including an accepted (`processed`) one. The granted roles are not returned; read them with the `pinecone_role_bindings` data source using `principal_type = "invite"`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    pinecone = {
      source = "pinecone-io/pinecone"
    }
  }
}

provider "pinecone" {
  client_id     = "your-client-id"
  client_secret = "your-client-secret"
}

# Look up a single invite by ID. Unlike the pinecone_invites list, which returns
# only pending and expired invites, this also returns an accepted ("processed")
# invite.
data "pinecone_invite" "example" {
  id = "your-invite-id"
}

output "invite_status" {
  value = data.pinecone_invite.example.status
}

# The granted roles are not returned by the invite endpoint. Read them from the
# role bindings list instead.
data "pinecone_role_bindings" "for_invite" {
  principal_type = "invite"
  principal_id   = data.pinecone_invite.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The unique ID of the invite.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The timestamp when the invite was created.
- `email` (String) The email address the invite was sent to.
- `expires_at` (String) The timestamp when the invite expires if not accepted.
- `processed_at` (String) The timestamp when the invite was accepted. Null for pending or expired invites.
- `status` (String) The lifecycle status of the invite: `pending`, `expired`, or `processed`.
